title: Apple GPU prefill direct 8x16 ownership control
question: How does changing from one SIMD group per scalar output to one thread per output in an 8x16 threadgroup tile affect prefill projection timing before shared-memory staging is introduced?
hypothesis: At larger M, abundant independent outputs may make a one-thread-per-output mapping competitive by removing SIMD-group reductions and scheduling 128 outputs per threadgroup. Serial K accumulation, incomplete row tiles, and lower per-output parallelism may dominate at small M.

baseline.ownership: One 32-lane SIMD group owns one scalar output.
baseline.reduction: FP32 lane accumulators followed by warp.sum

control.ownership: One 128-thread group owns an 8x16 output rectangle; one thread owns one scalar output.
control.reduction: Each thread accumulates K serially in one FP32 register.
control.edge_policy: Bounds checks cover incomplete M and N tiles.
control.purpose: Hold output ownership constant for the subsequent shared BK=32 staging experiment; never promote this control directly.

unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output
FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
no weight packing or quantization change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each benchmark implementation's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Committed torch.nn.Linear short-prefill oracle M=3 K=33 N=5
Exact output tile M=8 K=32 N=16
Qwen KV width M=8 K=896 N=128
Existing decode, packed-QKV, and two-output tests remain passing
correctness.gate: All finite numerical comparisons pass the frozen linear tolerance before timing.

workload_matrix.primary_interpretation_workload: The rotating packed-QKV curve, because hot repeated weights are exceptionally cache-favorable.

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_linear_prefill.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0007 --run-id EXP-0007-RUN-001 --direct-comparison --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0007-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and workload, control median divided by baseline median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and control faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and control slower in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.production_decision: None. This is an attribution control, not a dispatch candidate.

nonclaims: No shared-memory, BK-blocking, or tiled-input result.
No cache, bandwidth, occupancy, or scheduling mechanism claim from timing.
No end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.
No dispatch threshold is selected from this control experiment.

decision.next_experiment: Compare this exact 8x16 ownership mapping against BK=32 shared X and W staging so the incremental effect of explicit tiling is identifiable.
